artifact: DAPFAM P1 measured CPU baseline package
boundary: Artifact-only review of the validated aggregate P1 package. No protected split membership, qrels, query IDs, rankings, per-query outcomes, provider payloads, final evaluation, or external evidence was accessed.

strengths: The package measures family-level Recall@100 for the preregistered R0 and R0-W CPU baselines on train and selection only.
OUT Recall@100 is explicitly tagged primary while ALL and IN remain secondary diagnostics.
The package requires exactly four arm/split slots, twelve aggregate metric rows, fixed top_k=100, and hash-bound request, receipt, manifest, and validation artifacts.
Each slot passed JSON schema, content commitment, Git commitment, manifest commitment, request-receipt binding, and aggregate-only boundary checks.
The evidence is limited to P1_CPU_BASELINE, R0/R0-W, and train/selection; it does not claim R1 improvement, held-out confirmation, legal validity, or publication readiness.
The receipt preserves active_final_872_global_untouched as not_claimable and the final split remains closed.
The source contract, request commit, aggregate receipt, four manifests, four validation reports, and MLflow registration form one traceable hash-bound chain.
R0 is family-first SQLite FTS5 BM25 and R0-W is deterministic 512-token MaxP under the same evaluator and top-k contract.
The fresh package does not promote the superseded legacy receipt, and historical exposure remains explicit.
The protected runner repeated every slot and rejected any determinism mismatch before accepting the receipt.
suggestions: Retain the transient MLflow launcher failure in the append-only session capsule as an operational failed attempt, without changing the measured package.
weaknesses: Operational failed attempts are intentionally outside the immutable measured package and must be preserved in session provenance.

strengths: The run used 45,336 families, 250 train queries, 125 selection queries, fixed lexical retrieval, exact family aggregation, deterministic duplicate execution, zero paid cost, and no GPU or model download.
All four manifests bind the same 10,835.0971197-second aggregate execution and immutable external index/evidence stores.
suggestions: Add privacy-safe progress reporting with stage, processed/total, elapsed time, and bounded ETA for future long-running executions.
weaknesses: The accepted package records only total latency and completion; it has no non-protected stage heartbeat for live operational monitoring.

findings.evidence_locator: receipt.latency_seconds and package slots; no progress artifact or heartbeat contract is present
findings.observation: The run exposes accepted aggregate completion and total latency but no privacy-safe live stage or processed-count telemetry.
findings.reasoning: This does not invalidate the deterministic metrics, but it prevents precise ETA and stall diagnosis during a multi-hour CPU run.
findings.suggestion: Emit interactive progress for TTY users and structured non-TTY heartbeats containing only stage, processed, total, elapsed_seconds, and bounded eta_seconds.

overall.one_line_summary: The fresh P1 CPU package is structurally valid, reproducible, aggregate-only, and sufficient to close P1 while keeping P2 unstarted and final-872 closed.
strengths: Accepted receipt with zero blockers and twelve aggregate metrics across the exact four required slots.
All four validation reports are valid with every declared structural check passing.
The run is CPU-only, offline, zero paid cost, and hash-bound to source commit 947d9a132f2272774dcd8b4ab6e831e0734ec7d3.
MLflow mirrors one parent and four children without protected artifacts.
weaknesses: Live execution observability was limited to operating-system process counters because the runner had no privacy-safe heartbeat.

requested_decision: Promote the validated P1 baseline facts, mark P1 complete, and mark P2 ready but not started; do not open D2 or D3.
